name: Cherie Ho

papers.title: MessyMem: Learning-from-Doing Memory for Mobile Manipulation
papers.abstract: Mobile manipulators deployed at home across many rooms and many visits should improve with experience: after failing to open a locked cabinet, or finding an object in a drawer, the robot should use that knowledge to avoid repeated mistakes and complete future tasks more efficiently. However, today's robots often treat each task as new. Currently, compact scene representations omit interaction-derived knowledge, raw video buffers quickly grow to become inefficient and difficult to query, and VLM planners reason at inference time without persistently updating what the robot knows. Memory for mobile manipulation must be spatially grounded and queryable, updatable from interaction, and fine-grained enough to surface visual context that a text summary would lose. We present MessyMem, a memory system that enables mobile manipulators to learn from doing by building a compact 3D scene graph and associating it with learned interaction-derived properties and keyframes for visual detail. A task planner can use this memory to avoid repeated failures, reuse object locations, and recover visual context for long-horizon decisions. We evaluate MessyMem across multiple tasks in simulation and on a real mobile manipulator, showing that persistent interaction-grounded memory significantly improves long-horizon task success over representative baselines.
topics: 视觉语言动作与基础模型

papers.title: MessyNav: Zero-Shot Navigation via Manipulation in Messy Environments
papers.abstract: Real-world environments are messy. Paths are often blocked by everyday objects like chairs and toys, requiring interactive navigation (the ability to alter the environment to clear a path) rather than standard navigation alone. Existing methods rely on extensive simulation-based learning or per-scenario instructions specifying which objects to avoid or manipulate. They struggle to generalize across novel objects, diverse environments, and varied contexts such as a cart of fragile glassware that should be avoided while an empty one can be pushed. We formalize this problem as open-world interactive navigation and present MessyNav, a zero-shot framework based on vision-language models (VLMs). At its core, MessyNav performs explicit VLM-based affordance reasoning before task planning to decide whether to push, pick up, or avoid an object and produce a high-level plan. Deployed on a mobile manipulator across multiple real-world indoor and outdoor environments, MessyNav achieves substantially higher success rates than existing baselines without any task-specific training.
topics: 视觉语言动作与基础模型
